methodology: Ranked by (1) strength/decisiveness of the measured result, (2) reproducibility (own official benchmark/test suite reproduced > custom-but-real experiment > partial), (3) evidence quality (independently re-measured with tiktoken/real subprocess exit codes, not trusting a vendor's self-reported number). Mixed-result candidates (a real win alongside a real failure) are ranked on their strongest genuinely-measured claim but flagged, not hidden.

ranking.rationale: Most decisive, cleanest result of the entire pass: 1/8 -> 8/8 real concurrent-git success rate, at trivial overhead. Fully reproducible with nothing but git itself -- zero external dependency, zero license question, zero blocked toolchain.

67.5x (conservative lower bound) token reduction, measured against this session's own real, current tool definitions -- as close to zero-inference-distance evidence as this pass produced. Already deployed in StealthLab, so this is confirmation of existing value, not a new-adoption bet.

77.0% real token reduction on StealthLab's own code, independently tiktoken-measured, deterministic (no embeddings/API needed for this command), Apache-2.0, prebuilt binary reproducible by anyone in minutes.

9/9 of the project's own real unit tests pass at the pinned commit -- the strongest reproducibility signal available (the artifact's own test suite, not a test I invented), MIT-licensed, mechanism located precisely in source.
Same evidence quality as C06 (shared test run, same commit, same license); ranked just below it only because it is the less load-bearing of the two techniques for StealthLab's own architecture.

Real, reproduced against StealthLab's own 176-file backend/app using the project's own official no-DB benchmark. Ranked below the top 5 only because the benchmark deliberately excludes the query layer (needs Memgraph, not tested) -- the number proven is 'parsing+graph-construction is fast and works,' not the full retrieval value proposition.

Ranked last among survivors specifically because it is the one candidate with a real, measured, negative finding alongside its real positive one: 92.8% token reduction is genuine and strong, but the tool's own hook-latency benchmark shows it breaching its own documented SLA by ~35x in this real environment, unfixed by installing the accelerator. Selected because the core token-value claim independently holds, not because the latency problem is dismissed.
